item.title: Enter WebMCP: The Agent of Change
item.description:
AI agents interacting with your website can do much more than browse. They might purchase a product, evaluate your marketing materials while helping someone understand the competitive landscape, or complete a task for a potential customer. Those are just the obvious examples.

The mistake is to think of an agent as another visitor clicking around your site. An agent can evaluate options, connect information, make recommendations, and take action on behalf of the person it serves. That creates a different kind of opportunity for businesses.

item.title: Veeva CRM Is Leaving Salesforce. What You Do Next Decides Your AI Layer.
item.description:
For most of its life, Veeva CRM has been a Salesforce application. The objects, the Apex, the reports, the mobile app, the integrations, the admin skills: all of it sat on the Salesforce platform. Veeva is now moving CRM onto its own Vault platform, and it has said that support for the Salesforce-based version runs through 2030.

That sounds like a long runway. It is not. Every life sciences company running Veeva CRM has to make the same move in the same window, using the same limited pool of people who have done it before. The companies that size the work now get to choose their timeline. The ones that wait will take whatever timeline the market has left.

Chicago IL • March 1, 2026. Mach Five Tech today announced a strategic product and platform partnership with Bet Max Action to design, build, and scale a tournament-based sports gaming platform focused on fan engagement, flexibility, and rapid deployment across markets.

The partnership centers on the development of Bet Max Tourney, a full-stack tournament application, and supporting platform infrastructure that enables Bet Max Action to launch, test, and iterate quickly while supporting future integrations with sportsbooks, media partners, and international operators.
